The solicitation document and incorporated provisions and clauses are those in effect through the RFO. The associated North American Industrial Classification System (NAICS) code for this procurement is 541511 - Custom Computer Programming Services. The small business size standard is $34.0 Million. This is an unrestricted competition. Both small businesses and other than small businesses under the applicable size standard are eligible to respond. DESCRIPTION OF REQUIREMENTS Background The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) Engineering Laboratory (EL) supports the advancement of Additive Manufacturing (AM). As AM transitions from prototyping to industrial production, the seamless integration of AM machines with enterprise software specifically Manufacturing Execution Systems (MES) is the primary enabler for increasing throughput and addressing scalability issues. However, the standards are missing for interoperable AM and MES integration. The research team at the System Integration Division has a research objective to develop a neutral information model that can be standardized for A

deliverables_scope.text: ’s Administration (VA) Office of Research and Development, Regional Procurement Office – East in Pittsburgh, PA intends to negotiate on a sole source basis with Psychology Software Tools based in Sharpsburg, PA on behalf of the VA Salt Lake City Healthcare System. The requirement is to: Acquire 25 new Phantom systems manufactured by Psychology Software Tools, which may include storage and shipping when delivery is required. Engineering services to provide inspection, calibration, maintenance, Geometric Disk upgrades, and other upgrades to 105 currently installed Phantoms and up to 25 additional systems. The new Phantoms shall meet/exceed the specifications below and be 100% compatible with Phantom systems currently in-use at the VA facility. Website Development Services for the continuation of a project website already prototyped in collaboration with Psychology Software Tools. The systems will be used on an ongoing VA research study on Traumatic Brain Injuries (TBI). A Phantom is a precisely manufactured object of known size and composition that is imaged to test, adjust, or monitor; a Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) system’s homogeneity, quantitative precision, and shape geometry for the purpose of quantification and correction of both measurement accuracy and quality. Phantoms attach to M

ers to collect and calibrate diagnostics for brain imaging. The VA research office currently uses phantoms supplied by Psychology Software Tools and must continue to use the same phantoms to maintain the integrity of research results. Too many variables from other systems can skew research data and some include proprietary magnets which are not compatible with the current system. The Phantom systems require calibration to the necessary proprietary format and require anisotropic diffusion, which is critical to diffusion imaging required by VA research. a. Acquisition of Geometric Distortion Disks for 100 Existing Phantom Devices. The minimum specifications are: Multiple geometric test points and patterns across a plane of the magnetic field Features support assessment of B1, B0 non-uniformity, geometric linearity, slice profile and slice positioning accuracy, resolution and SNR, etc. b. Additional MRI Calibration Phantoms – Universal. The minimum specifications are: Phantom enclosure filled with deionized water with multiple internal test disks (1) Anisotropic Diffusion Disk 20+ anisotropic diffusion test points containing hollow micron scale (< 1 micron inside diameter) textile fibers– Taxons™ to simulate diffusion characteristics of human axons for assessment of FA, AD, RD, MD. ADDITIONAL SERVICES ON NEWLY ACQUIRED DEVICES Service, Recondition, MRI Calibration Phantom: Return of unit service after 1 year of use for evaluation, reconditioning/recalibration, and component upgrades. Includes free upgrade of any internal components to any improved models/revisions. Storage & Shipping: Secure temperature-controlled storage of inventory units for up to one year with multiple shipments to test sites as directed. The requirement will take place at a VA facility in Salt Lake City, UT. INTRODUCTION AND OVERVIEW Summary: The United States contains more species of turtles than any other country – accounting for approximately 20% of turtle species richness globally. These species face increasing pressures, particularly from illegal collection and international trade. Demand for U.S. turtles remains high in East Asian markets for use as pets, food, and medicinal ingredients. While federal and state law enforcement agencies are skilled at intercepting trafficked turtles, a critical limiting factor remains: the lack of sufficient capacity to house, evaluate, and safely return confiscated turtles to the wild. This pro

nforcement agencies are skilled at intercepting trafficked turtles, a critical limiting factor remains: the lack of sufficient capacity to house, evaluate, and safely return confiscated turtles to the wild. This project addresses that need by piloting a structured turtle management system in partnership with U.S. States and Tribes, with the goal of responsibly repatriating turtles to the wild. This effort will enhance the long-term conservation resilience of native turtle populations and help stop the loss of American wildlife to illegal markets abroad. Overview: Wildlife professionals broadly agree that U.S. native turtle trafficking volumes have escalated to crisis levels over the past decade. Large-scale seizures involving hundreds of turtles are now common. U.S. species most frequently encountered include box turtles, spotted turtles, and mud and musk turtles, along with other high - risk species such as wood turtles, bog turtles, and diamondback terrapins. Not only does trafficking undercut domestic conservation efforts to protect our native wildlife, but it removes important ecological engineers from our landscapes, responsible for seed dispersal and nutrient cycling. Federal and state law enforcement agencies devote substantial resources to combating illegal turtle

Center (LaRC) requires the purchase of Allen-Bradley ControlLogix 5590 Controller, ControlLogix L73 Workstation components, EtherNet/IP communications modules, ControlLogix chassis, Stratix 2500 and Stratix 5800 industrial Ethernet switches, and the FLUKE 1773 Power Quality Analyzer which are required to integrate directly with the existing Rockwell Automation architecture. Purpose: The purpose of this memorandum is to define the minimum salient characteristics required for the procurement of three (3) Custom Mobile Marksmanship Training Simulator Systems at Luke AFB, AZ. Any proposed equal system or components must meet or exceed the specifications detailed in this document. 2. The simulator must be a fully mobile, modular system designed for rapid deployment, capable of supporting both dryfire and simulated recoil training weapons. OVERVIEW The Defense Health Agency Contracting Activity (DHACA), on behalf of the Program Executive Office Defense Healthcare Management Systems (PEO DHMS) Joint Operational Medicine Information System (JOMIS) Program Management Office (PMO), is seeking information on modernized, cloud-capable solutions for efficient, adequate, and reliable medical modeling and the development of realistic scenario and plan-based estimates. The JOMIS PMO requires a solution configurable for full joint interoperability. This joint medical planning capability must satisfy baseline requirements for survivability, patient safety, and quality of care during major combat operations, such as anticipated Large-Scale Combat Operations (LSCO), as well as Defense Support of Civil Authorities (DSCA), Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief (HADR) missions, and multi-domain operations below the threshold of conflict. Reliable, agile casualty predictions support the timely flow of patient care. This end-to-end process includes: 1. Treatment of patients from Outside the Contiguous United States (OCONUS) Point of Injury (POI). 2. Transport and en-route care between theater hospitals. 3. Inter- and intra-theater patient movement

uiring additional forces to accomplish assigned contingency plan mission objectives. A modernized medical modeling application in a cloud environment will facilitate the seamless sharing of medical planning and modeling data across multiple systems RFI for JOMIS Medical Planning, Modeling and Simulation Capabilities 2 CUI//PROCURE CUI//PROCURE throughout the entire Military Medical Enterprise (MME), reducing operational costs, increasing resiliency, reducing risks, and providing timely planning and decision-making. These capabilities must be rapidly and globally aligned and/or reconfigured to respond to the changing operational requirements of Combatant Commanders (CCDRs). The Joint Medical Planning Tool (JMPT) and Medical Planners Toolkit (MPTk) are the current legacy medical planning capabilities. These tools are computer-based applications slated for migration to a cloud environment during FY26. In parallel, JOMIS is initiating efforts to modernize these legacy capabilities. Requirements for the modernized capability will be established by the Office of the Joint Staff Surgeon.
